---
title: "About"
---

I am a PhD student in the School of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University (Computational Biology Department), advised by Dr. Jose Lugo-Martinez. I build machine-learning systems for **agentic scientific discovery**, **autonomous laboratories**, and computational biology.

My lab-automation work includes:

- closed-loop serial-dilution experiments spanning a liquid handler, plate reader, robotic arm, and monitoring cameras;
- readiness and safety checks, including confirming that a plate is present and correctly oriented before transfer;
- agent-driven evaluation of dose-response curves and reruns with an adjusted concentration range; and
- **simPCL**, a simulator and benchmark generator for planning and fault recovery in programmable cloud laboratories.

During the limited [Model Hardware Standard (MHS)](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-hardware-standard-research-preview) research preview (announced by Anthropic), I led CMU's work using MHS and built the drivers and orchestration for those physical instruments. [Read the full case study.](posts/2026-08-27-mhs-preview.qmd)

Before CMU, I completed my Master's at Bilkent University under Dr. A. Ercument Cicek, where I developed generative models for biological sequence optimization. My work has been published in venues including ChemBioChem, PLOS Computational Biology, and Bioinformatics Advances.
